PCIF1-mediated m6Am RNA modification of WNT/FGF signaling pathway components in mesenchymal stem cells is necessary for normal osteogenic differentiation and bone formation, as its loss impairs osteogenesis by destabilizing Wnt11, Fzd4, and Fgfr2 mRNAs through reduced cap-proximal m6Am methylation, which can be rescued by activation of downstream Wnt signaling.

PCIF1-mediated m6Am RNA modification in mesenchymal stem cells is essential for bone formation because it stabilizes WNT signaling pathway transcripts (Wnt11, Fzd4, and Fgfr2) to maintain osteogenic differentiation, and loss of PCIF1 function causes impaired osteoblast differentiation and reduced bone mass that can be rescued by RSPO2-mediated WNT pathway activation.
